The paths, working guidelines and rubric are in the Obsidian note. This page gives you a workspace with everything loaded and a starting template for each path.

| Path | Question | Deliverable |
|---|---|---|
| **A** · Western blot | Your own densitometry, or the course CSV as a dry run | Manuscript figure + stats and methods paragraphs |
| **B** · Binary classification | `ISLR2::Default` or any binary outcome with n ≳ 500 | Held-out ROC, calibration, cost-based threshold |
| **C** · Simulation study | How badly does the MLE behave under separation, and does Firth fix it? | Bias and coverage curves + recommendations |

Write your analysis plan (model, contrasts, multiplicity, exclusions) **before** you run anything below.

## Path A template: western blot

Runs on the included CSV. To use your own data, paste it in as a data frame with the same columns (Genotype, Bio_Rep, Tech_Rep, Target_Intensity, Loading_Control_Intensity).

```{webr}
#| caption: Path A template
#| max-lines: 40
d <- read.csv("data/western_blot_example.csv") |>
  mutate(Ratio    = Target_Intensity / Loading_Control_Intensity,
         Genotype = factor(Genotype, levels = c("WT", "HET", "KO", "RESCUE")))
d_bio <- d |> group_by(Genotype, Bio_Rep) |> summarise(Ratio = mean(Ratio), .groups = "drop")
print(table(d_bio$Genotype))                          # n per group = biological replicates

fit <- lm(log(Ratio) ~ Genotype, data = d_bio)        # prespecified: log scale
anova(fit)
emm <- emmeans(fit, ~ Genotype, type = "response")
contrast(emm, method = "trt.vs.ctrl", ref = "WT") |> summary(infer = TRUE)   # ratios vs WT

ggplot(d_bio, aes(Genotype, Ratio)) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.12, size = 2.5, alpha = 0.8) +
  stat_summary(fun.data = mean_se, geom = "errorbar", width = 0.2) +
  stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "crossbar", width = 0.45) +
  labs(y = "Target / loading control (a.u.)")
```

## Path B template: held-out logistic regression

```{webr}
#| caption: Path B template
#| max-lines: 40
set.seed(2026)
idx   <- sample(nrow(Default), 0.7 * nrow(Default))
train <- Default[idx, ]; test <- Default[-idx, ]

fit <- glm(default ~ balance + income + student, family = binomial(), data = train)
tidy(fit, exponentiate = TRUE, conf.int = TRUE)

p_test <- predict(fit, newdata = test, type = "response")
auc(roc(test$default, p_test, quiet = TRUE))          # held-out AUC

# calibration: observed default rate within deciles of predicted risk
cal <- data.frame(p = p_test, y = test$default == "Yes") |>
  mutate(bin = ntile(p, 10)) |>
  group_by(bin) |> summarise(predicted = mean(p), observed = mean(y))
ggplot(cal, aes(predicted, observed)) + geom_abline(linetype = 2) + geom_point(size = 2) + geom_line()
```

## Path C: explore separation before you simulate properly

n = 20 observations and one binary predictor with true log-odds ratio β. Watch how often the ordinary MLE "escapes" (|β̂| > 10) as β grows. The full study also fits `logistf` and tracks coverage; start from the workspace below.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof sep_beta = Inputs.range([0, 5], {value: 2, step: 0.25, label: "True β"})
viewof sep_n = Inputs.range([10, 100], {value: 20, step: 2, label: "n"})
```

```{webr}
#| input:
#|   - sep_beta
#|   - sep_n
#| caption: Separation explorer (500 simulations)
#| autorun: true
set.seed(99)
x <- rep(0:1, length.out = sep_n)
est <- replicate(500, {
  y <- rbinom(sep_n, 1, plogis(-1 + sep_beta * x))
  suppressWarnings(coef(glm(y ~ x, family = binomial()))[2])
})
ok <- abs(est) <= 10
cat(sprintf("MLE escaped (|b| > 10) in %.1f%% of fits\nmedian estimate when finite: %.2f (truth %.2f)\n",
            100 * mean(!ok), median(est[ok]), sep_beta))
hist(est[ok], breaks = 40, main = "Finite MLEs", xlab = "estimated β")
abline(v = sep_beta, col = "red", lwd = 2)
```

## After the capstone

You now have a workflow for the four biggest situations in applied research: continuous outcomes and group differences (Modules 3–4), binary outcomes (Module 7), counts with varying exposure (Module 8), and non-independent observations (the mixed-models part of Module 8). For what's not covered: survival analysis (`survival`), Bayesian regression (`rstanarm`, *Regression and Other Stories*), and multiple testing / FDR (`p.adjust(method = "BH")`).
